html:
The Soufriere Hills volcano on Montserrat began erupting in July 1995 after centuries of quiet. The eruption has gone on, with pauses, for decades.

Ash and pyroclastic flows buried the capital, Plymouth, and the south of the island became an exclusion zone. On 25 June 1997 flows killed 19 people who had stayed in their villages.

About two thirds of the people left, many to Britain, where the British government gave them the right to settle. Those who stayed moved north. The Montserrat Volcano Observatory now watches the mountain, as scientists do on Mount Pelee and other Lesser Antilles volcanoes.
